name: git_status
description: Repository head refs, current log version and landing policy.

name: git_refs
description: Branch refs, optionally as of a past log version.

at.description: Read as of this transaction-log version (time travel)

name: git_log
description: First-parent history of a branch, newest first, with landing versions. With path, only commits that changed that path (or anything under a dir/ prefix).

at.description: Read as of this transaction-log version (time travel)

name: git_txlog
description: The hash-chained transaction log: every ref move with paths, read set and actor.

name: git_show
description: One commit: message, parents, changed paths, checks, reviews, landings and landing gates.

name: git_merge_base
description: Best common ancestors of two commits.

name: git_ls_tree
description: List a directory at a commit, branch or past version.

at.description: Read as of this transaction-log version (time travel)

name: git_cat_file
description: Read one file at a commit, branch or past version. UTF-8 text is returned as text, other bytes as base64. On main without commit or at, it reads main's published head, which can trail a landing by a few seconds; to read your own landing, pass the version git_land returned as min_version (STALE_READ while main has not reached it: retry).

at.description: Read as of this transaction-log version (time travel)

min_version.description: Read main at this transaction-log version or later (read-your-writes after git_land)

name: git_get_objects
description: Fetch immutable Git objects by id and kind (tree entries, commit headers, blob bytes as base64), in order, up to a response budget. Resume with after=next. Start from a commit's tree and request only the subtrees and blobs you need (sparse by construction). Path-restricted tokens must pass commit and each object's path inside their grant.

name: git_grep
description: Search file contents and paths at a commit, branch or past version (case-insensitive with ignore_case). Uses a trigram index partitioned by top-level directory and reused across commits; results list matching lines per file.

path.description: Only paths starting with this prefix

name: git_blame
description: Line-by-line attribution of a file on a branch: the commit that last changed each line, from the file's first-parent history.

name: symbol_list
description: Symbols (functions, types, methods, modules) in a Rust, TypeScript or JavaScript file at a commit, branch or past version, each with a handle for symbol_edit. A parse failure is reported, never hidden.

name: symbol_get
description: The source text of one symbol (by qualified path like Type::method, or name) with its handle. Read only what you need instead of whole files.

name: git_diff
description: Files changed from base (default: head's first parent) to head, optionally with unified patches. merge_base compares against the common ancestor, like base...head.

head.description: A 40-hex commit id or a branch name (default main)

base.description: A 40-hex commit id or a branch name (default main)

at.description: Read as of this transaction-log version (time travel)

name: git_commit
description: Create a commit on the server from file changes against a branch head (or an explicit parent). Nothing is landed: the commit is recorded and must pass checks and review before git_land moves a branch. Declare read_set (paths, dir/ prefixes, or path#symbol entries such as src/lib.rs#Policy::backoff for the symbols you relied on) so concurrent work is checked for independence; the platform derives which symbols your change wrote.

name: symbol_edit
description: Replace one symbol's source on the head of a branch, creating (not landing) a commit. The handle must still match the symbol in the current file; a stale handle (the symbol changed or vanished) is rejected. The edited file must still parse.

name: symbol_contract
description: The contract governing one symbol at a commit, branch or past version: inputs, outputs, effects, errors and invariants. status is authored (a recorded contract matching the symbol's current node digest), derived (from the signature and doc comments) or stale (a recorded contract exists but the symbol changed since; it is reported, never served as the contract).

symbol.description: Qualified symbol path like Type::method, or a name

at.description: Read as of this transaction-log version (time travel)

name: symbol_contract_record
description: Record an authored contract for the symbol a handle names (from symbol_get, symbol_list, symbol_contract or symbol_view). The handle must match the symbol at its commit; the record binds to that commit and the symbol's node digest, so it turns stale when the symbol changes.

contract.description: Typed contract; every field optional, at least one stated

name: symbol_view
description: Agent view of one symbol at a revision: its source and handle, its governing contract, and its graph neighbors (callers, callees, members) with handles. Neighbors are resolved lexically by name within the files you can read, so treat them as candidates.

symbol.description: Qualified symbol path like Type::method, or a name

at.description: Read as of this transaction-log version (time travel)

name: git_codemod
description: Literal find/replace across a branch (optionally under a path prefix), computed partition by partition and reduced into one commit (not landed).

name: git_plan
description: Plan proposed work items at one revision of a branch (nothing runs). Items whose symbols share a reference cycle that one of them writes are joined into one item; the rest are staged so items in one stage are independent (neither writes what the other reads or writes) and an item that reads what another writes comes after it. Reads are extended with the symbols their symbols reference (closure_depth). Items with a base_version report stale reads since then. Symbol entries on unparsed files are planned at path level.

at.description: Log version to plan at (default now)

items.description: A path, a dir/ prefix, or path#symbol_path
A path, a dir/ prefix, or path#symbol_path

name: git_check
description: Record a check result for an exact commit (requires the check scope).

name: git_check_run
description: Ask the platform to execute the policy's check runners on an exact commit (all runners, or one by name). Runs also start automatically when a commit is recorded; results appear in git_show.

name: git_session_record
description: Record which coding session produced a commit you pushed (needs write; only the commit's pusher or the repository owner): the CLI (e.g. claude-code, codex, opencode), the model, a summary of at most 4 KiB (refused if it holds a credential), optional SHA-256 hex digests of the prompts and of the declared read set, and an optional transcript_ref (a URL or opaque id; transcripts are never uploaded), and an optional session_id naming the coding session (e.g. opencode:ses_…) so its records across commits tie together. Posting the same record again answers the first.

name: git_sessions
description: The session records of a commit, oldest first: cli, model, summary, prompt and read-set digests, transcript_ref, session_id, who recorded each and when.

name: git_sessions_recent
description: The repository's session records newest first (default 50, at most 200): commit, its message's first line, cli, model, summary, session_id, how many reads the commit declared, who recorded each and when. Filter by session_id (one coding session), cli, model or ref (the sessions behind a branch's commits); pass next as before for the following page.

name: git_context
description: What a coding session starting work should know, in one read: main's head (and branch's, when named), the landing rules, the newest session records (what earlier sessions did), open change requests, and the newest authored symbol contracts, those on paths first.

name: git_bisect
description: Find the first commit on a branch that breaks a policy check: start with good, bad and check (a policy runner name); the platform runs the check on midpoints and narrows the range as results arrive. Pass id to read progress.

name: git_pin
description: Pin (or unpin) a commit so vacuum never releases its objects, for example while a long job reads it.

name: git_review
description: Approve or reject a commit (requires the review scope; authors cannot review their own commits; rejection needs a reason).

name: git_merge
description: Create (not land) a merge commit of source (a branch or commit id) into branch `into` (default main), using a three-way merge on the server. Returns up_to_date or fast_forward when no merge commit is needed. Conflicts return CONFLICT with diff3-marked text per path to resolve in a follow-up commit. into may be a branch or a commit id. With on_conflict "workspace", conflicts return a two-parent workspace commit with every cleanly merged path (conflicted paths keep into's content) plus the conflicting paths, instead of CONFLICT.

name: git_revert
description: Create (not land) a commit on the server that undoes a commit's changes relative to its first parent, on top of a branch head. Fails with CONFLICT when the branch changed those paths since; reconcile with a three-way merge instead.

ref.description: Branch whose head becomes the parent (default main)

name: git_cherry_pick
description: Create (not land) a commit on the server that re-applies a commit's changes on top of a branch head. Fails with CONFLICT when the branch's versions of those paths differ from the commit's parent.

ref.description: Branch whose head becomes the parent (default main)

name: git_rebase
description: Rebase a working branch onto another branch's head (default main) on the server: replays the branch's commits not on onto, oldest first, each as a three-way merge, then moves the branch with one compare-and-swap on its planned head. Requires the write scope. A conflict returns CONFLICT with base/ours/theirs per path (details.conflicts, plus details.commit) and leaves the branch unchanged; a branch already on onto answers up_to_date; a push to the branch meanwhile returns STALE_HEAD. Protected branches (main) are refused; merge commits on the branch return NOT_SUPPORTED.

onto.description: Branch whose head the commits replay onto (default main)

name: git_branch
description: Create or move a working branch (any branch except main) to a recorded commit, by compare-and-swap: expected is the branch's current commit, or null to create it. Requires the write scope; a mismatch returns STALE_HEAD. main moves only through git_land.

name: git_tag
description: Create a tag (refs/tags/<name>) at a recorded commit; with message, an annotated tag (the platform builds the tag object, tagged by tagger or the caller). Tags are immutable: creating the same tag again is a no-op, a different one under an existing name returns ALREADY_EXISTS, and no tool moves or deletes one. Requires the write and land scopes. The tag is logged like a branch move, listed by git_refs (annotated tags under annotated, ref name to tag object id), served to git clone (with the peeled commit) and mirrored to the object store. Annotated tags pushed with git push are accepted too, as is a tag object given as object_b64. REST: GET /tags/<name> answers a tag's commit and its tag object (data_b64) when annotated. REST: POST /tags.

message.description: Tag message: makes an annotated tag

tagger.description: Tagger identity of an annotated tag (default: the caller)

object_b64.description: An annotated tag object made elsewhere (git tag -a), base64: kept byte for byte; it must tag commit

name: git_land
description: Move a branch to a commit that passed its required checks and approvals (requires the land scope). If the branch moved meanwhile, the platform merges on the server: independent or cleanly mergeable work lands as a platform merge commit (post-land checks run on it); a stale read or textual conflict returns CONFLICT with details. With fast_forward_only, the commit lands only if its first parent is the current head; otherwise STALE_HEAD, and nothing is queued or merged. Returns the landing's transaction-log version: reads of main that pass it as min_version see the landing at once, while main's Git commit is projected shortly after (git_commit is null until then). Landing a branch's head on main marks that branch's open change request landed in the same transaction.

name: git_fork
description: Fork this repository: a new repository owned by your account, its branches and tags this one's at the current version, its history shared (nothing is copied; objects are read from this repository). Needs read on the whole repository (directly, as a member, through a team, or because it is public) and an account credential (a session or a personal access token with repo:admin), never a repository token. Open a change back with git_change_create {fork, branch, title} on this repository. A repository with forks cannot be deleted until they are. REST: POST /fork.

owner.description: An organization to own the fork (you must be one of its owners); default your own account

visibility.description: The fork's visibility (default private, whatever this repository's is)

parent_version.description: This repository's log version the refs were copied at

name: git_change_create
description: Open a change request: propose landing a branch on a base branch (`base`, default main; another existing branch). The branch must exist and not be main or a release branch; a branch has at most one open change (ALREADY_EXISTS otherwise). Approve or reject with git_review on the head commit and land with git_land {ref: <base>, commit: head} (approvals and required checks gate a protected base such as main; another base takes the write scope); a new push moves the head, so earlier approvals stop counting. Needs the write scope and a whole-repository credential. From a fork: pass `fork` (the fork's id) and a branch of the fork; this needs only read here and write on the fork, the branch's new commits are carried into this repository and the change proposes their mirror forks/<fork>/<branch> (it follows later pushes when shown). REST: POST /changes.

base.description: The branch to land on (default main); must exist and differ from branch

fork.description: A fork of this repository whose branch is proposed (call on the parent)

outputSchema.description: A change request: a branch proposed for landing on base.

base.description: The branch the change lands on (main unless another was named)

head.description: Open or closed: the branch's current commit (null once the branch is deleted). Landed: the commit that landed.

source_repo.description: A change from a fork: the fork's repository id

source_branch.description: A change from a fork: the fork's branch (mirrored here as forks/<fork>/<branch>)

name: git_change_list
description: Change requests, newest first, filtered by status (default open). REST: GET /changes?status=&limit=.

change.description: A change request: a branch proposed for landing on base.

base.description: The branch the change lands on (main unless another was named)

head.description: Open or closed: the branch's current commit (null once the branch is deleted). Landed: the commit that landed.

source_repo.description: A change from a fork: the fork's repository id

source_branch.description: A change from a fork: the fork's branch (mirrored here as forks/<fork>/<branch>)

name: git_change_show
description: One change request: the change, its head commit's record (git_show's shape: checks, check_runs, reviews and landing gates), its comments (oldest first), its branch's pushes from the transaction log (newest first) and the diff from the merge base with main to the head (git_diff's shape; for a landed change, against main just before it landed). patch adds unified patches. REST: GET /changes/:number?patch=1.

head_commit.description: git_show's answer for head (null when the change has no head)

base_protected.description: Whether landing on the base needs the head's gates (main and release branches); another base lands with the write scope

diff.description: git_diff's answer: {base, head, changes} (null when the change has no head)

change.description: A change request: a branch proposed for landing on base.

base.description: The branch the change lands on (main unless another was named)

head.description: Open or closed: the branch's current commit (null once the branch is deleted). Landed: the commit that landed.

source_repo.description: A change from a fork: the fork's repository id

source_branch.description: A change from a fork: the fork's branch (mirrored here as forks/<fork>/<branch>)

comment.description: A comment. With path, line and side it is anchored to a line of the diff at commit: side old is the base file, new the head file (patchRows old/new line numbers).

push.description: One move of the change's branch from the transaction log.

name: git_change_comment
description: Comment on a change request (body at most 8000 bytes; credentials are refused). path, line and side anchor it to a diff line at commit (default: the change's head). resolve marks every unresolved comment on that anchor resolved, with or without a new body. Needs the write or review scope and a whole-repository credential. REST: POST /changes/:number/comments.

comment.description: A comment. With path, line and side it is anchored to a line of the diff at commit: side old is the base file, new the head file (patchRows old/new line numbers).

name: git_change_close
description: Close an open change request without landing it (the branch stays). Its author, the owner or a holder of the land scope may close it. REST: POST /changes/:number/close.

outputSchema.description: A change request: a branch proposed for landing on base.

base.description: The branch the change lands on (main unless another was named)

head.description: Open or closed: the branch's current commit (null once the branch is deleted). Landed: the commit that landed.

source_repo.description: A change from a fork: the fork's repository id

source_branch.description: A change from a fork: the fork's branch (mirrored here as forks/<fork>/<branch>)

name: git_change_reopen
description: Reopen a closed change request. Its branch must still exist with no other open change. Its author, the owner or a holder of the land scope may reopen it. REST: POST /changes/:number/reopen.

outputSchema.description: A change request: a branch proposed for landing on base.

base.description: The branch the change lands on (main unless another was named)

head.description: Open or closed: the branch's current commit (null once the branch is deleted). Landed: the commit that landed.

source_repo.description: A change from a fork: the fork's repository id

source_branch.description: A change from a fork: the fork's branch (mirrored here as forks/<fork>/<branch>)

name: git_release_create
description: Publish a release for an existing tag: a title and notes, then assets with git_release_asset_upload. One release per tag (ALREADY_EXISTS otherwise). Needs the write and land scopes and a whole-repository credential. Sends the release.published webhook event. REST: POST /releases.

name: git_release_list
description: List releases, newest first, each with its tag, commit and asset count. REST: GET /releases.

name: git_release_show
description: One release: title, notes, tagged commit, assets (name, size, sha256, content type) and, for an annotated tag, its tag object id, message and tagger. REST: GET /releases/:tag.

name: git_release_delete
description: Delete a release and its assets; the tag stays (tags never move or disappear). Needs the write and land scopes. Sends the release.deleted webhook event. REST: DELETE /releases/:tag.

name: git_release_asset_upload
description: Attach a file to a release (at most 4 MiB here as base64; up to 25 MiB with REST PUT /releases/:tag/assets/:name and the raw bytes as the body). Assets are immutable: a name is used once per release (ALREADY_EXISTS), at most 20 per release. Answers the recorded size and sha256. Needs the write and land scopes.

name: git_release_asset_download
description: Read a release asset (at most 4 MiB here; larger ones with REST GET /releases/:tag/assets/:name, which answers the recorded sha256 in x-yoneda-sha256). Answers the bytes in base64 with the recorded size and sha256.

name: git_hook_list
description: Webhooks of this repository: id, url, events, paths, active, consecutive failures and undelivered count. Secrets are never listed. Needs the owner or repo:admin.

name: git_hook_create
description: Add a webhook: signed POSTs (X-Yoneda-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of the body with the secret>, X-Yoneda-Event, X-Yoneda-Delivery) to a public https url for each event, in log order, at least once. Events: land, merged, refused, branch (created/moved/deleted), tag, check (conclusion pass/fail/error), change (change requests: X-Yoneda-Event change.opened, change.commented, change.landed or change.closed; titles and comment text only for hooks without paths), release (release.published or release.deleted); all when omitted. paths limits commit messages to commits inside those paths. Returns the secret once. Needs the owner or repo:admin.

name: git_hook_delete
description: Delete a webhook; undelivered events are dropped. Needs the owner or repo:admin.

name: git_hook_deliveries
description: A webhook's last 50 delivery attempts, newest first: delivery_id, event, attempt, ok, HTTP status, ms, error. Needs the owner or repo:admin.

name: git_member_list
description: Members of this repository: account, role (read, write, land or admin), added_by and added_at. The owner is not listed. Needs the owner or an admin.

name: git_member_add
description: Add an existing account as a member, or change its role. Roles: read (read and clone); write (also commit, push branches, post checks); land (also review and land on protected refs); admin (also act as the owner, except deleting the repository and managing admins). A member's personal token holds only what both its scopes and the role allow. Only the owner grants, changes or removes admin. Needs the owner or an admin.

name: git_member_remove
description: Remove a member; its access ends at once. The owner cannot be removed. Needs the owner or an admin (only the owner removes an admin).
